The source procedure supplies its costs, application triggers, target eligibility, saves, frequency, concentration and endings; a component ID alone grants nothing. Alternative modes never apply together merely because both IDs appear in a binding. ## Records, clocks and precedence Each application records its identity, exact source, owner character, target, selected mode/components, application order, recorded source DC, deadline/marker, concentration or attachment relationship, remaining uses, and applicable immunity/suppression. Display names never create conditions or prerequisites. An owner's mark cannot satisfy another owner's class hook. A corpse marker, map point, archived spell, intrinsic Oracle Curse and hard-denial history are distinct state types. Explicit operative effect text controls over a less-specific summary duration field. Use preserved regular-turn markers for **next** turn and bare N-round durations as in the combat guide; an in-progress current turn is not the next turn. Unqualified next turn refers to the source; explicit its/target refers to the target. Bare hostile N rounds, including hostile marks, use N future target regular ends. Beneficial/self N rounds use source regular starts. Preserve virtual markers through initiative changes and absence. Out of initiative bare N rounds use application+6N seconds, retaining that deadline on entering initiative. Explicit source/concentration endings still apply. **NEW current-turn bridge:** “end of that turn” or the supplied bare “end turn” effects end at the end of the actual turn containing the application event, including another creature's or an extra turn. With no current turn, use application+6 seconds. An application during end-turn resolution expires at that same end after resolving, rather than acquiring a fabricated next turn. This applies to Resonant Seed, Winter's Embrace, Frost Totem and Glue. It does not override an explicit next-turn endpoint. The reference represents an expiry as an ordered `(seconds, phase)` marker, preserving exact rational seconds from the combat clock. Every turn-end deadline uses expiry phase 20: current actual turn, source/target next regular end, Nth future target regular end, and Balanced Elements' following target end. End-trigger application/resolution occurs at phase 10 and the next event slot at phase 30. The effect therefore remains during final end events and expires afterward at that same second. Turn-start and absolute elapsed deadlines use phase 0. Callers must choose an explicit typed deadline; bare numeric expiries are rejected. No fractional-second workaround or duplicate turn is created. Repeat saves, ordinary duration expiry and previously reviewed periodic/recharge clocks use regular turns unless an explicit exception applies. This is **not** a global rule changing every “each turn” damage trigger. Zone entry/start application checks, repeat ending saves and once-per-numbered-round caps are distinct events. Follow each source's actual trigger and cap; concentration alone grants no recurring application save. ## Speed arbitration **NEW:** Keep soft flat reductions, soft fractional reductions, explicit Speed0 controls, and Core Grappled/Restrained separate. Terrain changes movement cost; it is not a Speed penalty. “Hostile soft control” means an adverse control record regardless of whether an enemy, ally or the victim applied it. 1. Determine each possessed mode's Speed after compatible ordinary bonuses and systemic flat penalties (including serum/expedition Strain, serum side effects, cargo and stances). Their existing stacking rules still apply. 2. Evaluate every unsuppressed adverse soft-control record against that **same** pre-control Speed. Flat -10 gives `max(0, Speed-10)`; half gives `floor(Speed/2)`; use the exact registered formula for other records. 3. Use the lowest result. Different slows do not add unless an expressly reviewed source grants an exception. Keep all losing records and their independent deadlines. 4. Apply separately established global multipliers such as Exhaustion's half-Speed. Apply an active Hypermutation floor as specified below. 5. An explicit Speed0 state, Core Grappled/Restrained, Exhaustion5 or another actual immobilization overrides the numeric result. An unavailable mode remains unavailable. A separate prohibition on voluntary movement is not removed by a positive Speed. Thus -10 and half on Speed30 yield15; Exhaustion then yields7. Two -10 records yield20, not10. Serum/expedition penalties remain independent system penalties, not competing hostile slow records. A minimum attached to a penalty cannot raise existing Speed: Iron Leash Aura uses `min(preSpeed, max(5, preSpeed-10))`. Active adverse soft controls and explicit source Speed0 controls carry `eligibility.slowed-foe`; Core Grappled/Restrained alone, Prone, cargo, terrain and Exhaustion do not. A numerically overshadowed application still qualifies. Suppressed, expired or prevented applications do not. Same owner/target/group/exact profile refreshes without adding magnitude or shortening its remaining deadline. Different magnitude/formula profiles retain separate deadlines within a group; a weaker later application cannot erase an unexpired stronger one. Removing/suppressing one record exposes any other valid record. Paid reapplication and source caps remain required. No arithmetic Speed result grants movement: the combat guide's common spent-movement ledger still applies. ## Mage Cold and elemental extension One owner group `mage.cold-focus:<owner>` contains passive/Bolt/Surge flat profiles and Glacier profiles. A single hit invoking both the passive and Bolt/Surge does not create duplicate penalties. The current Cold Focus passive requires positive actual cold damage from a qualifying Cold Mage spell. Bolt/Surge explicitly apply their Cold rider on a legal hit even if damage is reduced to0. Glacier's failed-save profile does not require positive damage. A currently impossible/ineligible instruction claims no budget; proceed to the next. Compatible requirements can share one genuine legal execution. A single Action satisfies two instructions only if that same Action actually fulfills both. Once an earlier valid instruction claims an indivisible ordinary Action/interaction, an incompatible later instruction receives no second copy. Movement uses only the actual remaining movement allowance; sequencing instructions cannot reset spent movement or violate an earlier still-maintained posture/restriction. A losing ongoing instruction is ineffective only for its contested budget/opportunity, not automatically dispelled. Its compatible independent portions may still operate within existing permissions. Its own endpoint, replacement and saves remain. Priority loss never refunds hard-control history. An invalid later order cannot erase an earlier mandate merely by being issued. Example: Grovel and an Attack Action may both be satisfied if Prone uses only legal movement/posture and the attack remains legal. Two incompatible ordinary Actions cannot both be demanded from one Action budget. This arbitrates actual compelled behavior; it does not make compulsion optional or restore unavailable actions. ## Six-second control cadence outside initiative This NEW cadence binds Dire Charm and Crown of Madness's ongoing order/end-save procedures. This treats application during an outside-initiative cycle like application during an existing regular turn, preventing repeated casts from creating extra immediate Actions. A readied spell commits this casting sequence at preparation; release has no second cast, cost, cadence update or Counterspell window. Countering requires an actual operational spell or class card, its repertoire/access and a legal remaining Reaction. The ordinary Counterspell is now reviewed; it is separate from the Mage and Wizard class cards. Dispel Minor, Dispel Resonance, Dispel Magic (Lesser) and Dispel Magic use their exact individual scopes. Rank-limited dispels inspect the original generating cast's spell rank, not RP cost or the dispeller's rank. Higher and unassigned source variants retain their own unfinished status. ## Counterspell checks and interruption The [exact notebook review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_ABJURATION_RANK2_3_EXACT_REVIEW.md) confirms this authored timing interface and corrects the earlier binary-check proposal using the existing [Core roll rules](CORE_RESOLUTION_PLAYTEST.md). This is a tabletop procedure; the pricing helper does not implement nested reactions. Ordinary Counterspell uses its casting class's actual spellcasting ability + PB against **DC 10 + twice the triggering spell's actual rank**. The class Wizard/Mage cards retain their printed Intelligence + PB check and PAT Resonance Influence 42670 ion caster still affects that caster's own effective orientation normally. If Lock/Anchor is applied while Purge or Suggestion is already effective, it snapshots the currently effective defined value; later ending/suppression of the lower overlay does not alter that snapshot. When Lock/Anchor ends or is inactive because a zone was exited/suppressed, the then-live lower lawful result becomes effective immediately with its original deadline/history; no old snapshot is restored and no missed application replays. Undefined axes are never fabricated. The [complete fifteen-spell AC4 chapter](../spells/candidates/ABJURATION_CONJURATION_RANK4_REVIEWED_03.md) and [review receipt](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/AC4_EXACT_ACCEPTANCE_03_RECEIPT.json) govern the exact accepted authored procedures, including separate Alignment Anchor placements, finite summon profiles and all scoped interfaces. These manuscript acceptances do not enable runtime selection or certify human balance. **Resonance Influence:** compute ordinary legal spell price first, including mandatory extras, Dissonance, eligible source reductions/waivers and each feature's own minimum. Then apply final plus/minus1, minimum0. A feature's minimum1 reduction step is not a universal final-price floor. Ease can offset one RP of the resulting total, including a mandatory Resonance Shield extra. A genuine RP-priced spell reduced/waived to0 still qualifies; Burden makes it1. In Mage Spell Sharing, the Mage's earlier sharing payment is unchanged, while the ally's later actual shared spell is independently priced: Ease0/Burden1. An ally unable to pay cannot commit, leaves Influence pending, and still uses the original limited sharing window. Nonspell techniques and charge-only spells without an RP-price interface do not qualify merely because they have costs. Qualifying class discounts require their actual class/spell eligibility; examples do not reclassify nonspell techniques.       - generic: matches.append((str(p.relative_to(root)), s))
